C-REVIEW-SURFACE.Summary: Create the review check surface — mechanized pattern detectors and process audits with deterministic finding IDs, a multi-surface corpus scorer for D4, a determinism/no-regression CI gate with a falsification witness, detached-reviewer skill text and read-only tool allowlists, and a published host-capability matrix with honest degradation.
C-REVIEW-SURFACE.Problem:
The pipeline is [LLM generates] → [deterministic verifier] → [policy gate] → [execute/apply]. Box 3 (gates) shipped in Phase 5. What produces the review content that apply requires is still honor-system: two archived bundles (C-GATE-SURFACE, C-GATE-RECORD-ABSENCE) hold self-recorded pass verdicts written by the implementer through ngrace gate verdict (A33.3). The gate cannot tell a self-review from a detached one, and D11 only requires a recorded verdict's existence.
§6.4's four process audits (scope, test weakening, backward-compat, hunk coverage) and the defect corpus's nine review-surface expected findings are about different things. The corpus names exact codes — review.confidently-wrong, review.self-referential-comparison, review.regex-over-structure, review.zero-or-more-swallow, review.unthreaded-construct — that no catalog emits at e5627ca. A scorer written only against §6.4's audits would report zero detection on all nine review rows while every audit passed its own tests: a measuring instrument pointed at nothing (D4).
A27.2 and A34.1 hand a build order: the unknown-value query, the counterpart query (parameterized over four concrete list-pairs from Phase 5), and the differential harness. Those cover confidently-wrong and unthreaded-construct well and leave self-referential-comparison, regex-over-structure, and the silent zero-or-more half as separate detectors (A35.2 corr 72).
src/review/ does not exist. Role presets under ngrace-setup-subagents/references/roles/ carry no tool allowlists. README.md has no host-capability or degradation language. CI has no determinism or corpus gate. D16 requires the determinism gate be observed failing once.

Goals.Goal: An invocable review surface: ngrace review, registered from src/grace.ts, implemented under src/review/. It runs mechanized detectors and emits deterministic finding IDs; it does not author status or write Verdicts (invariant 8 / F1; Phase 5's ngrace gate verdict remains the recorder) (A35.2 corr 81).

Detector set is the A35.3 superset: (A) five pattern detectors emitting the exact corpus review.* codes; (B) four process audits with distinct review.* codes; (C) join engine with A34.1's four pairs as first fixtures. No family silently dropped (A12.4 / standing rule 7).
Deterministic finding IDs stable across reruns and across unrelated edits (blank line above a finding leaves the ID unchanged). Never line-number-only, timestamps, or narration.

Multi-surface corpus scorer over corpus() (11 entries, 18 expected findings at e5627ca): lint, health, and review dispatched by finding.surface; both directions (mustFire true missed and mustFire false fired) (A35.2 corr 70, 82; D4).
Determinism + no-regression gate wired into validate:* / CI, with a falsification witness that demonstrates red when a detection is deliberately broken (D4, D16, A35.2 corr 83).
D14 boundary one surface over: runLint never emits review.*; the review surface does (A7.2 both directions; A35.2 corr 73, 77).
Detachment contract in ngrace-reviewer and a read-only tool allowlist on the reviewer role preset(s), reported verbatim; enforcement is host-side where the host supports it (A35.2 corr 74; §5.2).
Host-capability matrix published in README.md with degradation for cold subagent spawn and tool-level read-only stated plainly (A35.2 corr 75).

Constraints.Constraint: src/lint/core.ts does not learn about review. review.* codes live in src/review/catalog.ts (D14).
ngrace review does not write Verdicts, Decisions, status attributes, or archive paths. Recording stays on ngrace gate verdict (F1, A35.2 corr 81).

Decided (A36.1): the corpus stays at 11 entries this phase. Process audits are proven by unit fires/silent pairs and §0.7.2's mutation check. Seeding process-audit rows is owed only if a process audit regresses in content while the determinism gate stays green.

Decided (A36.2): a join-engine finding takes a review.<pattern> code only when it is an instance of that pattern as the corpus defines it. Otherwise it is process-shaped and takes a family-B code. Resemblance is not the test; the corpus entry is. Family B never moves the pattern trend.
Full grace mutate / revert-and-rerun is out of scope (Q1, A35.2 corr 84). Hunk coverage is attribution only.
No new runtime dependencies. Surgical diffs only (§0.1).
Skill edits under skills/ngrace/ are mirrored to plugins/ngrace/skills/ngrace/ in the same commit (§12.2).
Detachment and tool-level read-only are conditional guarantees (§5.2). Do not claim them unconditionally in README or skill text.
Every new review.* code carries §12.1 evidence links (derivedFrom / proposedBy) where applicable.

Standing rule 10 (A30.6): review findings state their scope before any durable home is chosen. Default: ephemeral to the review run; do not invent a second ledger section mid-phase without an amendment.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Making the apply gate distinguish self-review from detached review. D11 requires existence of a recorded verdict, not toolkit-verified trustworthiness (A33.3, A35.2 corr 80).
Re-implementing lint-owned or health-owned corpus rows inside src/review/ (zo-01, ut-01, health markers).
Deterministic failure localization (Phase 7), selection (Phase 8), confidence/calibration (Phase 9), plan-quality/doctor (Phase 10), adoption (Phase 11).
Full mutate / differential revert-and-rerun as a required audit (Q1).
Making lint depend on run state or emit review.* / gate.* codes (D14).
Inventing a sixteenth track-level design decision (D1–D16 stand) (§12.5).

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REVIEW-OWN-SURFACE: Correction 81 (A35.2). ngrace review is registered from src/grace.ts and implemented under src/review/. It evaluates and emits findings with deterministic IDs; it does not write status or Verdicts. Discriminating negative: no review subcommand that calls recordReviewVerdict or sets status attributes.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REVIEW-D14-BOUNDARY: A review.* code is never present in runLint output (A35.2 corr 73, 77; D14). Integration test both directions per A7.2: review surface emits review.* on a seeded fixture; lint over the same tree emits zero review.*.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REVIEW-PATTERN-DETECTORS: A35.3 family A. The five codes review.confidently-wrong, review.self-referential-comparison, review.regex-over-structure, review.zero-or-more-swallow, review.unthreaded-construct each fire on their corpus mustFire:true review rows and stay silent on clean controls. The clean control for every entry is its own pre-apply() state, which build() produces lint-clean (A36.3 corr 85). Per-pattern fires/silent pairs reported (A35.2 corr 72).
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REVIEW-PROCESS-AUDITS: A35.3 family B. Scope, test weakening, backward-compat, and hunk-coverage audits each ship with distinct review.* codes (not the five pattern names) and a fires/silent pair. None requires the implementer's transcript (§6.7.3). Not folded into the five-pattern trend rate (A35.2 corr 71; A12.4).
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REVIEW-JOIN-ENGINE: A35.3 family C / A34.1. Parameterized counterpart (and unknown-value) query ships with fixtures for the four Phase 5 list-pairs: record scope×home, writers×commands, lint-catalog×benign readers, new-diagnostic×pre-existing artifacts. Each has fire and silent controls.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REVIEW-FINDING-IDS: Finding IDs are stable across two runs on an unchanged tree and unchanged when a blank line is inserted above the finding. IDs are not derived from line numbers alone, timestamps, iteration order, or agent narration (§6.4).
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REVIEW-SCORER: Scorer runs corpus() multi-surface (lint, health, review) and reports detection rate per pattern and per surface, both directions (A35.2 corr 70, 82; D4). Correction 85 (A36.3): every entry is scored twice — before and after apply() — because all four mustFire:false rows are lint-surface and the review surface would otherwise have zero silent-direction ground. A review.* finding on a pre-apply() tree is a false positive and is reported beside the after-state mustFire:false violations. Process-audit codes that are not corpus expected rows do not inflate pattern rates (A35.3).
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REVIEW-DETERMINISM-GATE: validate:determinism (or equivalent validate:* name) is wired into CI. Gate = two-run identity plus no-regression ratchet on previously caught seeded defects (D4). Falsification witness: a test deliberately breaks a detector or ID input and asserts non-zero / refuse; phase report shows that red output once (A35.2 corr 76, 83; D16; §6.7.1).
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REVIEW-DETACHMENT-ALLOWLIST: Reviewer role definition carries a tool allowlist with no write tool, reported verbatim (A35.2 corr 74; §6.4 non-negotiable 2). Skill text states detachment is host-conditional.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REVIEW-HOST-MATRIX: README.md publishes the three-layer capability matrix (CLI / skills / host adapters) and states degradation without cold subagents or tool allowlists (A35.2 corr 75; §5.2). No unconditional detachment claim.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REVIEW-NO-VERDICT-WRITE: ngrace review never appends to Verdicts or Decisions and never authors status (F1, A35.2 corr 80–81). Recording remains ngrace gate verdict.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Unit and integration tests for pattern detectors, process audits, join engine, finding ID stability, multi-surface scorer both directions, D14 boundary, and determinism-gate red witness; root lint 0 errors with C-REVIEW-SURFACE present; marketplace mirror check green; README host-capability section present; allowlist reported in phase report.

Assumptions.Assumption: Answered, not assumed: A36.1 accepts decision 1 (corpus stays at 11, with a named trigger for seeding process-audit rows later) and A36.2 accepts decision 2 with one clause — a join finding takes a review.<pattern> code only when it is an instance of that pattern as the corpus defines it; otherwise it is process-shaped and takes a family-B code.

Hosts that cannot enforce tool allowlists or cold subagent spawn remain usable: they record host-capability-missing (or form a non-detached verdict under project gateFailOn policy) rather than a disguised pass (D5, D11).
